key_insight: A compact set of consistent DNA methylation features can classify CNS tumors accurately and in an interpretable way across different sequencing platforms.
clinical_relevance: This could make routine neuro-oncology diagnostics more scalable by supporting reliable tumor typing from both array-based and sequencing-based methylation data.
method: Filtered CpG regions by variance and intra-/inter-class consistency
Selected informative features with elastic-net logistic regression
Trained a linear SVM and applied it cross-platform with missing-value imputation
evidence_signal: In external array-based validation cohorts (n=1,993), the classifier reached 0.96 accuracy and remained robust on bisulfite-equivalent targeted sequencing and Nanopore data.
watch_item: Cross-platform performance may depend on platform-specific preprocessing and imputation, so real-world deployment will need careful validation and quality control.
paper_title: Consistent DNA methylation patterns enable accurate and interpretable cross-platform classification of central nervous system tumors
